prompt: Six OSPF routers share one Ethernet LAN segment. How many full adjacencies form with a DR and BDR, compared with a full mesh? Assume broadcast OSPF network type, compatible configuration and fully converged adjacencies.

options.explanation: Correct. Four non-DR routers each form 2 (DR and BDR): 8. Plus DR–BDR: 9. A full mesh would be 6 × 5 / 2 = 15.
5 would be a star to the DR only, forgetting the BDR. And 30 counts each pair twice; the mesh is 6 × 5 / 2 = 15.
Every router still needs an adjacency to the DR and BDR; two adjacencies total would leave most routers out of sync.

options.text: 15 either way; the DR only reduces LSA size
options.explanation: Reducing adjacencies is the main purpose of the DR. Non-DR routers stay at the two-way state with each other.

workedExample:
```formula
A_mesh = n(n − 1) / 2
A_mesh = 6 × 5 / 2 = 15
A_DR = 2 × (n − 2) + 1
A_DR = 2 × 4 + 1 = 9
where
A_mesh: full adjacencies if every pair formed one
A_DR: full adjacencies with a DR and BDR
n: the routers on the shared segment, 6
In words: the 4 routers that are neither DR nor BDR form two adjacencies each, plus one between DR and BDR, giving 9 instead of 15.
```

The saving grows quickly: 20 routers gives 37 instead of 190.

prompt: An internal link in OSPF area 3 changes, altering a router LSA for that area. In which area's topology database is that LSA propagated and used for the area shortest-path calculation?

options.text: Every router in the whole OSPF domain
options.explanation: Router LSAs are area-scoped; the changed area-3 topology is not directly propagated throughout the entire domain.

options.text: Area 3, including the area-3 database of its ABRs
options.explanation: Correct. Other areas may receive inter-area reachability/cost changes, but do not receive area 3's internal router LSA as their own topology.

options.text: Only the two routers at the ends of the link
options.explanation: The changed topology LSA is propagated throughout its area, not just to the link endpoints.

options.text: Only area 0 routers, because the backbone computes routes for all areas
options.explanation: There's no central computation in OSPF. Each router runs SPF on its own areas' databases.

workedExample: The area-3 router LSA remains in area 3. Routers attached to area 3, including ABRs, use that area database to compute topology paths. Changed costs or reachability can affect inter-area advertisements and calculations elsewhere. Implementations may batch, throttle or incrementally calculate routes, so this does not require one full SPF execution for every individual flap or guarantee all impact remains inside the area. Configured aggregation can hide some changes, not every possible failure.
